summary: One main action with a menu of variations on it beside — Save, and Save as draft; Create agent, and Create and start. Two buttons, two tab stops, one shape.
useWhen: one action is the common case and a few variations of the same action are occasionally needed — save as draft, create and start, export as CSV
the variations would crowd the row as buttons of their own, and hiding the main action behind a menu would cost the common case a click

useInstead.when: the choices are different actions, not variations of one
useInstead.why: a split button promises its menu is "this, but slightly otherwise"; unrelated actions under it hide what they are behind the wrong label

useInstead.when: there are two actions of equal standing
useInstead.why: two visible buttons are faster than one and a menu, and neither is hidden

useInstead.when: the choice is a setting that changes what the main action does — the export format for every export
useInstead.why: a split button's main half always does the same thing; a remembered choice belongs in a control that shows it

composition.note: `label` and `onPress` are the main action; the children are MenuItems for the variations, each with a `key` that `onAction` receives.
composition.example: <SplitButton label="Save" onPress={save} onAction={(key) => key === 'draft' && saveDraft()}><MenuItem key="draft">Save as draft</MenuItem></SplitButton>

primary-brand.use: the default — the single most important action in a view; one per view, as for Button

primary-neutral.use: a primary action that should not carry brand colour

secondary.use: an action beside the primary, such as Export among a table's actions

lg.use: a page's single call to action

children.note: the variations; each names the whole action — "Save as draft", not "As draft"

requires: `label` — the main half's name and the group's name
guarantees: a `group` named by `label`, holding two Buttons that are two tab stops, the main one first
the menu half is named for itself and the action — "More options, Save" — so several split buttons on a page have distinct menu buttons
the menu half is a MenuTrigger: `aria-haspopup`, `aria-expanded`, ↓ opens on the first item, choosing closes the menu and returns focus to it
the main half always does the same action; choosing a variation never changes it
`isDisabled` disables both halves; `isMenuDisabled` only the menu, leaving the action; `disabledKeys` disables single variations
`type="submit"` makes the main half submit its form; the menu half never does
drawn as one button: one shared border at the seam, square inner corners, a square menu half; the focused half is lifted so its ring is not cut
in a stacked ButtonGroup it takes the full width, the main half growing
notes: a variation that is dangerous — "Delete permanently" beside "Archive" — should not share a button with a safe action; it needs its own confirmation
the menu's actions are reached through `onAction`, not through a submit: a variation that has to submit the form calls the same handler with its option, as the demo's wizard does

antiPatterns.dont: a main half that becomes whichever variation was chosen last
antiPatterns.do: the same main action every time
antiPatterns.why: a button whose meaning changes with history cannot be pressed with confidence, and a screen reader is not told it changed

antiPatterns.dont: a Button and an icon-only MenuTrigger placed side by side by hand
antiPatterns.why: the hand-built menu button is usually named only "More", has its own gap and radius, and is not grouped with the action it belongs to

antiPatterns.do: <MenuTrigger> with a Button named for what it opens
antiPatterns.why: "Actions" is not an action; pressing the main half has to do something
